title: Communism as a world movement
summary: After the Bolshevik takeover of Russia in 1917 and a civil war, the Communist International, or Comintern, was founded in Moscow in March 1919 amid proclamations of the end of the world capitalist order. At its Second Congress in July and August 1920, its leaders set twenty-one conditions for membership. Communist rule in Russia ended with the Soviet dissolution of 1991.

uncertainty.note: Begins with the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution and the March 1919 founding of the Comintern; 1991 marks the dissolution of the Soviet Union, the primary state patron of the world communist movement.

where.modern_name: Moscow, Russia (seat of the Comintern; the movement spread worldwide)
where.historical_name: Moscow, Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic

importance.justification: A revolutionary movement organized from Moscow that became a major force in twentieth-century politics.

related.because: The 1917 Bolshevik seizure of state power in Russia provided the territorial base, state resources, and ideological vanguard for a global communist network.
Marx and Engels's foundational manifesto provided the ideological theory of class struggle and international proletarian unity adopted by the world communist movement.
The global expansion of Soviet-backed communism and rival Western containment strategies initiated the four-decade Cold War confrontation.
